transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

I'm... just not feeling like myself lately. I don't know. I stopped doing things. Hiking, coaching, even playing my guitar... I just don't. People call and I don't call back. Mostly I just sit in my rental for hours. I know there are things I should be doing, but... I just can't make myself start.
How long have you been feeling this way—unable to do the things you normally enjoy and just sitting around?
A while, I guess. Um... maybe a year and two months. That's when I got this smaller rental. After the... after my divorce. Things just kind of unraveled since then.
During this past year and two months, have you felt persistently sad, empty, or depressed most days—or has your mood been relatively normal, with mainly just the loss of interest in activities?
I don't know about sad. I don't really... feel sad. It's mostly just... I just don't care to do anything. I don't know.
When you think about activities you used to enjoy, like hiking or playing guitar, do you still feel that you would enjoy them if you did them—or has the enjoyment itself gone away?
I don't know. I haven't tried. I just... I don't feel like picking it up. So I don't.
If I forced you to sit down and play your guitar right now, do you think you'd actually enjoy it while you were playing—or would it feel flat and pointless even while doing it?

I don't know... probably flat. I just... I don't feel like myself anymore. I used to do all those things... hiking, coaching, the guitar. Calling people. Now I just sit in the rental. For hours. I know I should do things, but... I just can't make myself start.
When you do manage to do something—like eating a meal or watching TV—do you find any enjoyment or satisfaction in it, or does everything feel kind of numb and empty?
I don't really notice. It's just... food. I don't think about whether I enjoy it. I just don't feel much of anything about it.

Before this past year and two months—before the divorce and the rental—have you ever had a period of time lasting weeks or months where you felt this same way? Where you lost interest in things, couldn't motivate yourself, and felt numb like this?
No. ... I don't think so. I was fine before. Just... since I moved.

In the years before you moved to the rental—say, in the 5 or 10 years before the divorce—did you ever go through a period where you felt depressed, lost interest in things, or struggled to get yourself to do things, even for a few weeks?
No. Like I said... I was fine. I just went to work, did my shifts. There was nothing wrong with me before all this.

When you were doing things before the divorce—like hiking or coaching—did those activities genuinely bring you pleasure or satisfaction at the time? Or have you never really felt that kind of enjoyment from them?
Yeah, I liked them. I mean... I wouldn't have done them if I didn't. It was fine.
Over this past year and two months, have there been days or weeks where you felt sad, down, or depressed—or has it mostly just been this lack of motivation and numbness without sadness?
I don't know about sad. I just... I just don't feel like doing anything. It's just flat. I don't really feel much of anything.
Over this past year and two months, have you noticed any changes in your sleep—like sleeping much more or much less than you used to? Or changes in your appetite?
Not really. I just... I sleep. I eat whatever. It hasn't changed.
In these past 14 months, have there been any days or stretches of time—even just a few hours—where your mood lifted a bit, you felt more like yourself, or you actually wanted to do something?
No... I don't think so. It's all just... the same.
